decks.name: Deathspeaker Self Mill (cornerstone deck)
decks.primer:
Yo! Welcome to the primer for my DS Self Mill Deck!

To start things off a quick history on me a tcgs and why im choosing this deck as my main passion project for the Sorcery tcg.


Basically for as long as ive been playing tcgs (started with Invasion block for mtg) ive loved using the graveyard as a resource. So naturally in mtg I was the reanimator guy and when I got a good collection I competed in legacy format events using a deck called Tin Fins and Dredge as a back up. I loved every minute of it too until mtg started doing things I heavily disagreed with and I dropped the game about 7ish years ago. When Sorcery was announced on KS it immediately gave me those mtg vibes I loved as a kid so I backed it. When I got my product I saw DS and knew this was the avatar for me and ive been working on making this deck as fun as I can so here we are haha.


So for the start behind this self mill deck is ever growing as I play more games against various avatars and opposing strats. The idea is pretty simple though, mill yourself to get that advantage asap. The advantage here is tons of card draw with those wizards and lots of minion generation with the necromancers. I also run a solid ordinary package that answers various problematic cards that exist in the game. The way I look at avatars is that each one offers the player a "cheat code" to help them win paired with piloting the deck correctly. DS "cheat code" is obviously using the graveyard as a second hand. When all this self mill stuff got printed in gothic my face lit right up and I felt at home haha. Something ive learned though is to not fill that yard up too fast, especially if the opponent is on fire, the bigger a yard you have the juicier a target it can become. Try to keep it minimal until you need new targets and go from there. In my maybe board I have a short stack of cards im considering and site hate is something ive added to it thanks to that unique fire site that kills my deck lol. Youll also notice I dont run ring, p stone, cores or other obvious "staple competitive cards" and I do that for a reason. I dont find those cards fun at all to play and im all about having fun here. If you want to run those no shame on you and feel free to edit the deck as you see fit to run the cards you want to run. Im choosing to run the token generating stuff to offer me good chump blockers or easy ping damage to opposing sites. Tokens in general are just annoying so it felt right to me and so far its been fun. Hotwheel has also been an all star for me. Killing random dudes or even putting in that finishing blow has been great. 3 might be overkill but I like running max copies of stuff when I can. I will say the mvp of the deck though is Skeleton Mage. I. Love. That. Card! Its so so good at everything this deck wants to do and casting Common Sense a million times in a game just feels criminal lol. But really it helps me always have an answer to my opponent with all the 1 of ordinary cards I run to be fetched with Common Sense. I also run some pet cards that happen to be very strong like good ol pudgy but besides that I tried making the deck with cards that function in my hand and graveyard to really abuse that "cheat code" I mentioned.


Hopefully this probably poorly written primer helps you all make your own sick DS decks and show my passion for the deck! So go out there and resurrect the realm in a fashion that fits you best!

decks.name: 1st Place Cornerstone w/Gothic (6-0) The Red Comet
decks.primer:
I registered for my LGS’s Cornerstone (we put in a lot of effort to get that status - should out to Battlegrounds in Richmond, VA!) but hadn’t played for five months. Going into the tournament, I needed 1) an Avatar I had at least some experience with 2) a deck that was pretty easy to pilot 3) something that could hopefully win or not make me look entirely foolish ;)


After looking at my old pre-Gothic decks, I landed on the “red deck wins” Pathfinder in a dusty deck box. I figured, “there have to be some cool new toys and more fire sites,” and I was pleasantly surprised. There’s a fair amount of Gothic in this deck as a result! I would add a Horns of Behemoth for the Wasteland if I had pulled one and I totally overlooked Vindictive Nation, which is also an easy add in lieu of one of the duals.


The Avatar pilots no differently than before, you have to attempt the optimal pattern to enable a path to at least six sites, but either via Giant, Warhorse, or just walking over a few sites, you can easily get to 10+ simply because of the tempo you have.


The deck archetype is classic sligh/red deck wins. You simply want to be as aggressive as possible. Gift of the Serpent, especially with Dragonettes, is AWESOME for taking out problematic minions. Searing Truth is an MVP as it gets you even more cards if you need them, but can also kill an Avatar instantly on DD. I’d definitely figure out a way to cut some things (I.e. Minor Explosion) to get up to max for each of those. I didn’t bother with any of the collection artifacts as they are simply too slow. The only collection card is a Hounds in case you elect to cast it from Molten Maar.


If you’re looking for something than can simply

blitz out a win, particularly before folks figure out deck efficiency and the meta, this may be a good choice for you. I’d you’re looking for something with some neat combos and cool interactions, there are a few, but really this is all about the burn. Enjoy the heat!

Hello,


**UPDATED DECK LIST**

https://curiosa.io/decks/cmjau0q4f57qozrfmy5yh22kc


﻿*** Deck is Obsolete because of Gothic and [[Druid]] nerf.***


This is my exceptional mono fire deck! The goal of this list is to put early pressure on the opponent with efficient minions, eke out card advantage where we can, and hopefully land a killing blow with a lucky burn spell.


We are aiming for a consistent and efficient early game. That is why the curve is low and does not include a lot of big finishers like [[Panorama Manticore]]. That is also why we are sticking with one element and not running Steam Druid. A big benefit of being mono fire is we get to run fun utility lands for extra value! 

  • [[Town]]: early ramp, a lot of the minions are exceptional and town will smooth out your early game.
  • [[Sinkhole]]: Removes problems like [[Pebbled Paths]] or [[Perilous Bridge]]. 
  • [[Wizards Den]]: Free card advantage-ish!!
  • [[Rift Valley]]: Sometimes deals with problematic sites, sometimes a free movement spell.

7 to 8 colorless sites seems to be the sweet spot if you consistently want to get (F)(F) early.



Mulligans 

Spells:

  • Mulligan all magic spells (except [[Pact with the devil]]... maybe), we want minions for early pressure.
  • Mulligan any finishers namely [[Rebecks]] & [[Boudicca]].
  • Remember what magic and finishers you mulligan, as they will not be outs later!!
  • Always keep [[Torshammer Trinket]].
  • Always keep [[Jihad]].
  • Don't clog your opening spells with lots of 4 drops if you don't have [[Town]].

Sites:

If your hand has a good curve of minions you can be very aggressive with Site.

  • If you are playing against control or earth dig for [[Sinkhole]] or [[smokestacks]].
  • [[River of Flame]] is one of the few answers to [[Root Spider]].
  • If your not playing against [[Archimago]] you can mulligan [[Funeral Pyre]].
  • If your not playing against [[Druid]] you can mulligan [[Arid Desert]].
  • [[Forge]] is strong in your opening hand, but you only need 1. 
  • If your opening hand is 3 (F)sites mulligan 1 or 2 unimportant ones in hopes of Hitting [[Town]] or [[Sinkhole]]. 
  • [[Town]] is super strong in your opening. 
  • Always mulligan [[Wizard Den]].
  • Its often poor to keep both [[Town]] and [[Sinkhole]], you will need (F)(F) early, use best judgment.


Game Play

Don't be afraid to play a [[Vile Imp]] or [[ Clamor of Harpies]] for no value. Its okay if [[Quarrelsome Kolbolds]] has to hit your [[Druid]] for 2, there is value in keeping up tempo and keeping your opponent under pressure. In that vain sometimes its okay to throw a [[Minor Explosion]] at the opposing avatar in the name of mana efficiency. Keep the games short and limit your opponents options. While the deck can play the value / control game (and sometimes you have to), we will often lose the late / long game.


It is usually correct to draw from your spell book. Only draw from your atlas if you can not make a play or REALLY need to double spell in a turn.


You can be pretty aggressive moving and attacking with your Avatar. You can double spell most the deck with 6 or 7 sites, so don't be afraid to skip a site draw or placement if you can get good value off it. Don't flip [[Druid]] unless it buys you a turn preventing a killing blow. Most of the time Tawny is more valuable.


"If you can be one thing, you should be efficient."




--------------------------------------------------------


Top 4 @ SCG Con Baltimore: Crossroads!

10-26-25


Notes from Baltimore:

  • [[Blaze]] under preformed. Low impact and bad against a flipped [[Druid]].
  • [[Clamor of Harpies]] plays well with [[Jihad]].
  • [[Clamor of Harpies]] teleport ability is mandatory, meaning you must move your tawny if there are no other legal targets.
  • [[Hillock Basilisk]] was amazing, and will 100% of the time cause a judge to be called.
  • [[Peasant Revolt]] was under whelming, buuuttttt seems important. (could be sooo good)
  • Super weak to an early [[ring of morrigan]] may want to run [[Shatter strike]].
  • The Atlas was great, all the utility site did work! And was never short on threshold!
  • [[Town]] is an MVP, can't stress this enough
  • this deck crushes other [[Druid]] decks especially steam :-)
  • using [[Clamor of Harpies]] to teleport a [[War Horse]] carrying a [[Siege Giant]], then having the [[Siege Giant]] throw the [[War Horse]] along with himself is my dream.
  • I had so much fun, and everyone I played against was so nice <3


1st Place @ Blue Moon Games: Cornerstone!

11-2-25


﻿Changes:

-1 [[Blaze]] +1 [[Minor Explosion]]


Wanted to get a 2nd copy of [[Hillock Basilisk]] in, [[Rebecks]] was okay but coasting 5 and dying to [[Peasant Revolt]] seemed like a fine cut. [[Blaze]] underwhelmed just added another [[Minor Explosion]] because Druid is everywhere.

Honestly [[Monstrous Lion]] and [[Hillock Basilisk]] kind of fill the same role I could totally see making that swap.
  • With so many Steam Druids running around [[Rift Valley]] hasn't been super useful, but Idk what site I would add in it place.

decks.name: Avatar of Air - 1st Place Cornerstone Championship
decks.primer:
This is a Gothic mid-range Air/Earth deck with Avatar of Air for mobility. It's not too different from the typical air/earth mid range gameplay that encourages an aggressive early-mid game with late-game finishers. With the changes to Guisarm and other "Strike" effects, you're not going for the OTK and instead looking to constantly apply pressure.


---------- Artfiacts:

Onyx Core is to help ramp and fix Earth Threshold. Torshammer Trinkets are to help deal more damage and make trades more favorable. Toolbox is to provide answers when you need them but more often than not it is to pull Zap! out from the collection to kill your opponent at Death's Door. You could argue running a 3 of to add consistency to access to the cards.


Rolling Boulder is a typical card to have in an Avatar of Air deck, however with Gothic we have a brand new toy to play with in Lord of Greed. You can now roll the boulder and have Lord of Greed bring it back at the end of turn.


---------- Minions:

Most minions don't' need explanation as they are typical valuable creatures to fly into your opponent's board with AoA.


Men of Leng is a personal pet card of mine that if played at the right time can be very hard to deal with and can take a few cards from your opponent. Use your Blinks, Wuthering Heights, and AoA to fling them to the back row and force some discards.


Skeleton Mage is a fantastic new addition to the roster of air minions as it not only lets you recast your magic, but you can also cast opponent magics that you may need (specifically says "a cemetery" not "your cemetery").


All of the ranged units become extremely difficult to play around with air's mobility. Stygian Archers are one of my favorite new additions. Kill stuff, gain benefits. Doesn't get more satisfying than that.


Daperyll Vampires are probably the most questionable minion on the list. With the changes to how they work in that you no longer get health when striking a site, they lost a lot of luster. However, they are still an airborne minion that is hard to deal with sometimes. They are the most likely to be replaced for lower-cost aggressive targets. And they've also been outclassed by one of my new favorite Airborne minions which are:


Legion of Gall are a fantastic minion. Never would they have printed a 5 mana 5 power Airborne unit in Beta, but they did it in Gothic and gave it an upside. These guys are a monster to deal with, especially early with a tower. On top of them dominating the air, they also remove cards from your opponent's collection. So you get to see what kind of answers they may have and remove their best options.


Lord of Fear is a game ender. Enemies can't defend alone is a huge effect and makes your offense feel so much more powerful. You get to trade better. You get to attack without being blocked. And most importantly Death's Door is scarier than ever.


Lord of Greed is an answer to your opponent's artifacts and he has an upside of having some fun synergy with Rolling Boulder. I debated over 2 of Fear over Greed but there are just too many good artifacts in this game that you want to shut them down as often as you can. We don't have Swap so this is one of our best and consistent answers to artifacts.


---------- Magic:

There are a lot of typical tempo spells you will see in a deck like this but there are a few cards that I want to talk about. Namely Gift of the Wolf and Vanishment.


Gift of the Wolf is a fantastic new card and I feel it might be overlooked very often at first glance. This card is so good at making trades, or just getting extra damage in with a ranged strike or site attack. The fact that it replaces itself and also is a great target for Skeleton Mage is what helped it earn its slots in the deck. I replaced Gigantism with this because Gift of the Wolf more easily fits into turns. Gigantism is still good, but often your opponent will have chump blockers making it have less opportunities to be used.


Vanishment is another one of my own personal pet cards. I like cards that replace themselves, and this does so and protects your board state. Plenty of times I find myself just ahead enough and Vanishment guarantees I stay ahead on my opponent's next turn most of the time.


---------- Sites:


My site choices are very defensive. Stuff like Perilous Bridge, Mountain Pass, and No Man's Land let you take advantage of AoA's mobility while shutting down your opponent's ability to strike back. The quality of sites drastically increased in Gothic. Double threshold sites are an amazing new addition. Learning how to mulligan sites is a process with this deck. Placement of air sites and defensive sites is something you will get used to after playing for a bit. Wuthering Heights is a new site that replicates AoA's ability. This lets you double fly units and get them further in to enemy territory.

Seeing Red

Primer by UnderSietch


*UPDATE*


I’ve updated this decklist to reflect the one I played in the SCG CON Baltimore 2025, where I took 1st place. I've also update the primer for the new list and added more specific examples of how I play special cards, artifacts and auras in addition to the turn by turn card flow breakdown. Thank you for your interest and your feedback!

Introduction:


I'm typically a very whimsical deck builder. I like the story and the artwork and the intricate interactions between the weirdest and coolest cards. I often even write a little bit of lore to explain the narrative of the "characters" in my deck and how they came together to do battle against strange and ominous enemies. What can I say? I'm a nerd.


But with the tournament season approaching, I've been noticing an uptick in a more competitive and aggressive play-style all around me. This deck is a response to getting my butt relentlessly kicked over and over by some very good players and deck builders in my local community, who were tuning their tournament decks at our casual meetups. The calculated and efficient competition deck is a new adventure and mindset for me. And I think a good amount of beginners luck, mixed with being thrown to the wolves (sometimes literally) again and again, led to my winning our NYC cornerstone recently. I had been so tilted, so often, that I was literally SEEING RED.


Philosophy:


I decided that I wanted to make my games as short and sweet as possible. I don't want to allow other decks to get set up and start to hit me with big, intricate plays. My goal is to get my opponent in a reactive space, having to spend their precious few actions each game removing my threats and adapting to my board position, rather than imposing their will.


Playstyle:


I chose Mono-Fire because it's a fast and nasty suit. There are plenty of places to find extra damage for removal and to lower my opponents life total, while leaving me in an advantageous board-state. And it's very low cost!


I chose the Druid as my avatar for one reason: An immortal, airborne spellcaster, TAWNY. Flying around and dealing Fire's unblockable Area of Effect (AoE) damage to both remove enemy threats and deal damage to enemy avatars simultaneously.


The basic idea behind the deck is to combine the sometimes self-destructing damage from tawny, and genesis damage from deserts, with genesis and end-of-turn bonus damage from fire minion cards to remove enemy threats and deal damage without spending mana or losing my minions in a fight.


For example:


Opponent plays an Autumn Unicorn on turn 3.

I attack it with Tawny (she dies, but there's one damage), I play a desert (one damage and summon Tawny again, she's back!), and I play a vile imp for 2 mana and the genesis damage removes the Unicorn and leaves my Imp and Tawny alive. The board now has two threats on it for me and none for them.


Tawny's bonus damage also works in the reverse. You can cast an AoE spell, then attack with Tawny to deal one damage to an enemy minion THEN cast a desert to deal one additional damage and summon Tawny again for no cost.


For example:


Opponent drops a Atlas Wanderers on turn 4 due to a Mana boost from a Gothic Tower.

I cast Firebolts with Tawny, then attack the Atlas Wanderers with Tawny dealing a 4th damage, then I tap my Druid to play a Desert nearby, dealing the Atlas Wanderers a 5th and fatal damage and summoning Tawny again for no cost.


This allows me to destroy my opponents 5-cost drop with a total expenditure of 2 mana.


The last and most important note I'll make about our magical owl friend is that she's actually the perfect foil to your Druid opponents. By using a Torshammar Trinket, you can still have Tawny fly around near your opponent's avatar when they are Flipped and Bruin is active. Now that she's a 2 power, she can take steps nearby your opponents Druid and not die from their special ability. Then, she can cast a kill spell.


Use your owl. Give it a Torshammar Trinket and hit your opponents sites as often as possible. Cast Boudicca and give Tawny a Trinket and hit your opponent's sites with your owl for 5 damage. Be very active and rude with your bird friend. If your opponent is spending cards and mana removing your owl, you are winning. They are spending time, energy and resource on something that you get for free. Try your best to get them to react to your owl.


For me? The Bruin is a "smash in case of emergency" card. I want to spend most games not needing it. I want to be able to cast tawny by playing a site all game long. She's that important.



How and when to play:


You need to be patient!

(read that again)


This deck allows you to win FAST. I've observed that, in many games, Sorcery players cast anywhere from 12-18 spells and it can take up to 50 minutes to finish. In my games, my opponents cast 7-10 spells and the game can be over in 25 minutes.


(Which resulted in a very nice long break between rounds for me at the tournaments)


That doesn't mean that you play all of your cards out fast, however. Quite the contrary. It means you need to make every point of damage count. Hit their sites and Avatars early and as often as possible, yes. BUT DO NOT EMPTY YOUR HAND. You are leading the action while tactically responding to their drops. Find ways to remove their drop and increase your board presence AND deal them a little damage each turn. It's very possible. But you are most likely playing only one spell per turn. Your owl, deserts, genesis effects and end of turn effects will make it feel like you're doing much more than that but you're not. It's very simple and very deadly. And you'll need spells in your hand if your opponent manages to slow the game down and draw things out.



Turn by turn:


Mulligan:


You want a removal or control spell like Disintegrate, Immolation or Infiltrate in your hand ideally, and at least one cheap minion and one fire damage spell. Having three minions isn't the end of the world. You can have a War Horse, Colicky Dragonettes and Saracen Raiders and play forward from a really good place. The removal and fire magics will show up when you need them.


Make sure you have a Forge and at least one Desert in your hand, trust me. If you can't do that, make sure you have two fire threshold in your opening hand. Sinkholes and Wizard's Dens are awesome, don't mulligan them unless you have multiples in hand.


Ideal sample hand:


Disintegrate, War Horse, Minor Explosion

Forge, Red Desert, Poison Well



Turn by turn breakdown:


Turn 1: play the forge, make the lance, create Tawny and have her pick up the lance.


Turn 2: If you went first, Play a Bonfire or a Funeral Pyre or something forward toward your opponent and drop the War Horse and step Tawny forward to hand the lance off to your other minion. You don't always get the charge or genesis effects of minions and sites to land, that doesn't mean it's a bad play. Remember you're increasing your board presence with each drop and they'll have to spend resources to clear those spells, which you'll replace with more powerful ones as you draw them. Of course the best sites to play forward in a central position would be a Sinkhole, Smokestacks or Vesuvius. But we can't always get what we want.


If you went second, try dropping that Poisoned Well and get a hit on their life total, if they played forward toward you. Or play a Sinkhole forward to prepare for any unwanted sites. Wizard's Den is also a fantastic starting site, or a drop on turn three on your back row to get the extra spell draw.


Going second also means you can bring the lance up from Tawny, hand it off to the War Horse and immediately step forward to deal 3 first-strike damage to either a minion or, ideally, your opponent's site.


NOTE: You will draw spells and play the sites from your hand on the first three turns.


Turn 3: I love the Redcap Powries here, or even a Trinket on Tawny and Firebolts for removal or direct damage to the enemy avatar (that's 5 damage turn 3). When in doubt, Minor Explosion is the best, most effective card in this deck. I honestly have considered adding a 4th copy recently. Explode everything all of the time. Do not hesitate to do damage. It's your whole job. Do it often. Colicky Dragonettes are good here. Save your Kobolds for later unless there's an obvious play that maximizes their end of turn strike ability.



Turn 4: You will draw and play a site. This leaves you with four sites on the board and three or four spells in hand. Great cards open up on this turn: Saracen Raiders is an awesome free 3 damage on an unprotected and unsuspecting opponent's site. Infiltrate becomes an option, but I typically save this until my opponent drops something that seems like a game-changing bomb. Think Pudge Butcher or Seirawan Hydra. These are the things you want to take and tap down and keep them out of the game. Redcap Powries with a Torshammer Trinket is a favorite of mine to remove a 4 power minion or strike a site for 4. Boudicca opens up on Turn 4, but don't drop her on the board unless Tawny and/or another minion can undoubtedly strike a site freely. Her ability is too good to waste. If you play Boudicca back and away from the fray, you may get multiple turns with her ability in play and swing the game heavily in your favor.



Turn 5: draw a spell and tap to draw a site. The only reason you would draw a site to play here is if you already have Rebecks in your hand and you see a good opportunity to use your charge giant to get a big hit in on your opponent. Otherwise, stick to the plan so you can have 5 sites next turn.


Turn 6: Draw a spell and play your 5th site. This should leave you with 3 or 4 spells in hand and five sites on the board. You can play everything in the deck besides Infernal Legion with this board state. This is where the world opens up to you. Try to spread your minions out as much as possible so that they're more difficult to remove. Your opponent is going to scratch and claw to stabilize. There may be temptation at times to play multiple cards from your own hand. Only do this if it lands your opponent at death's door or decisively swings the game toward your win.


Turn 7: Draw a spell and tap to draw a site. Now you have all of the sites that you'll ever need and you have three or 4 spells in hand. This is what I mean by BE PATIENT. You'll find yourself in a remarkable board state with plenty of spells in hand. If you can leverage your extra damage well, you might still have two or three threats on the board at this point.



How to Deal Damage:


Every time that you can, play a minion with charge and hit your opponent's sites. Every time that you can, cast fire spells that hit their avatar or groups of minions. By turn 5 or 6, you may have taken half of their life total away by chipping away with Tawny, fire damage and minions hitting sites.


I usually find that I'm holding more immediate damage threats than my opponent. If I consistently am hitting them once per turn for 3+ damage, I get them a little off their game and they start to have to waste resources and dig for answers.


Try not to win more. Win just enough. You really want those three spells in hand to deal with some of the game's inherent big swings.


How to win:


You didn't flip your Druid, did you? Good. Being able to summon Tawny (and maybe put a Trinket on her) and get her into position to deal a Minor Explosion, Firebreathing, Lava Flow, Firebolts or Firebreathing is your ticket to victory. Good players keep a kill in their hand when they can. If you can hold onto one of these spells and not use it until you get your opponent to death's door, you'll have a tidy and efficient victory on your hands.


Remove their threats when they're on death's door. Get rid of their minions, and clear your path. Sometimes you don't have the fire spell and you need superior numbers of minions to get a strike in. Don't forget to remove their blockers to make a charge minion very deadly.


Sometimes, walking your druid forward and then flipping for Bruin and your special ability, can pin their Avatar down when it's on deaths door and keep it from being able to run away from your fire damage. In this case only, you don't need Tawny, because your Avatar is your spellcaster.



Special cards and their uses:


Your damage (most of it) comes from your small minions and fire spells from Tawny. But sometimes you need to be able to flex into a more midrange role and become a bigger beast to seal the deal against a powerful opponent.


There are a few HUGE drops in this deck that help you out a lot.


Rebecks is my favorite card here, dealing 4 damage to an opponent's site on the same turn that you play it. Pair him with a Torshammer Trinket or Jihad for a bigger swing. Have him ride a warhorse to get him into a deeper and more problematic position for an opponent. On a later turn, use a fire spell to clear out a blocker before dropping Rebecks to get a free hit on your opponent's site.


Boudicca on turn 4 when you have Tawny and maybe a War Horse and a Redcap Powries on the board? Do some math here, that's 15 damage if they all go unblocked to your opponent's sites. Normally I play her very carefully away from the battle. But sometimes she can create a very welcome distraction. While your opponent focuses on removing her, you can keep hitting for 2-5 damage per turn on their life total. Remember the goal is to get them to door and ping them for the win. If you lose cards and life along the way, so be it. Don't win more! Just win. Never waste resources to save a special card.


Siege Giants are amazing. These guys are why I don't have to play Blaze or Mad Dash in this deck. I get all of the movement I need from these dudes. They can throw 21 of the cards in this deck (including Avatar and Tawny), to any nearby site without having to tap for the ability. They can even throw a War Horse that they themselves are riding. READ THAT AGAIN. They can saddle up on a horse, throw that horse diagonally, then both the horse and the giant still can take a step and declare an attack. Use Siege Giant to spread your damage out far and wide, like a joyful flaming trebuchet.


Monstrous Lion's job is actually as a removal spell. I use it to deal a surprise and tidy four damage to an enemy that's on my border or in my territory. Sometimes a BattleMage or some other antsy Avatar gets too close and catches a lion to the face. Don't expect the Lion to live for more than one turn very often. Add a Torshammer Trinket on turn 5 or later for extra Lion.


Askelon Phoenix is in the deck to provide air support and fire resistance. You'll very rarely use its ability to power it up. But it takes no damage from fire spells, minions or abilities. It survives a poison nova. Heck, it survives a direct strike from Ignis Rex holding Crown of the Victor. It's a good card, and is usually a sort of turret or defensive/support play for me, more so than a beatdown.


Infernal Legion has never been invited to a party. Nobody likes to see this thing hit the board. It's an absolutely enormous problem for most opponents. But be careful, it's also trouble for you if you don't play it right. This is another card I'd qualify as a late game or defensive bailout play.



Artifacts and Auras:


The Ring of Morrigan is the most efficient card in the game. I think it has to go in any deck right now. Its overall effect is that of a desert that can be triggered every turn and gains you life for each damage you do with it. Enjoy your bling.


Torshammer Trinket is very powerful. There is absolutely an argument for playing a third one of these in the deck and playing at 52 cards. Your opponent cannot interact with it unless they make you discard it from your hand. It can be placed on any minion or avatar in order to increase its power by 1 on your turn. Another little added single damage to reinforce the soul of the deck. Happy smashing.


Mask of Mayhem is a very tricky play. Be careful. I'd recommend dropping it when you have 2-3 minions nearby each other. Maybe one of them removes a large minion and the other two get a free hit that's big. If you can wipe the board and maybe follow it up with some Saracen Raiders or another charge minion? Go ahead. But be hyper aware that this also benefits your opponent. Battlemages love this being on the board and so do Avatars of Earth.


Drums of Doom is the one big defensive card I have in the deck. If all goes to heck and you need to protect yourself from minions, put Drums on your Avatar and flip for Bruin. Your thorns ability will now deal lethal damage to any potential nefarious trespassers.


Jihad - If you can cast Jihad on your opponent's side of the board, this deck gets very hard to deal with. This aura opens up all of your extra damage genesis and end of turn affects from minions, hitting the enemy's avatar the very first turn they're played. Don't hesitate to do damage to their life total. Take them to death's door as quickly as you can while not emptying your hand.



NOTE: I prefer to cast Jihad covering two of my opponent's sites and two of my own, so that I can summon non-charge minions and still receive the +1 power benefit.



The Great Famine very specifically removes the strongest minion in a four-square area at the end of your turn. Very often, the minions in this deck are less powerful than the average minion my opponent is wanting to cast. You can survive a turn or two under its protection and force your opponent to forego summoning in order to wait out your aura's duration. This is also our answer when someone has a big problem underneath of a site. This card also carries a very important word for our success in its text box: "occupying". This means that The Great Famine (and also Lava Flow!) can remove threats that are burrowed or submerged. So if you're struggling to remove anything from a Root Spider to a Great Old One with confidence, this is your huckleberry.



Dangers in the Meta:


Pebbled Paths, Bottomless Pit, Perilous Bridge, Troll Bridge, Gnome Hollows and Impenetrable Copse. Use your Sinkholes or Smokestacks of Gnaak in a center position to make sure you can negate these nasty sites.


Archimago. I don't know what to tell you. You will lose sometimes to someone who can cast Divine Healing 6 times during a game and then Craterize you twice. Get them to deaths door asap so that they can't benefit from healing.


Enchantress. I don't know about this one really, I'm just very afraid of how this avatar completely flips the physics of the board state. Control tends to trump aggro in these games. Speed is your best friend.


Water players or Steam Druids with Polar Explorers and Ruler of Thul. It's very hard to rush forward when you have to watch your back. I recommend sticking to the game plan and holding on to some AoE fire spells and Monstrous lions to deal with whoever decides to come in the back door with bad intentions.




IMPORTANT NOTE:


You're going to take damage during this game. Don't get me wrong, lots of time you'll be playing way ahead of slower decks. But I also won a lot of games in this tournament on double-death's door. Try to keep your cool. You've usually got more damage in hand than your opponent. Stay vigilant and trust that you can win. Stay ahead by a turn. Get your opponent to door first and use fire to finish it. Don't worry about the score, just the result.


One game, I went down to door when my opponent (another fast air/earth Druid) still had 12 life. I was so disheartened and I was sure my day was over. But he had played all of his cards that could deal damage to my Druid, which was safely nestled on my back row. I was able to infiltrate his Pudge Butcher and leave it ineffective while I flooded the board with spells from my hand. I still had 3 or 4 spells in hand and I had 6 sites down so I could drop two spells a turn to put the pressure back on him. It was a close one, and the high-heart-rate monitor on my watch went off twice. But I came back and won it.


Another game, an opponent stole my Infernal Legion using Infiltrate, then played a Grim Guisarme and Warp Spasm the next turn to hit me for 24 with it. Before this play, though, the score had been 20-2 in my favor. The Legion died and he had played all of his cards. I was able to stabilize and win in two turns.


In the finals of the Crossroads tournament final, I was down 18-2. And the 2 damage he had taken, he did to himself. Talk about a blowout. I managed the win because I stayed the course and made the best, most efficient plays. Eventually, I cleared his board and played enough threats of my own to deal two big swings and get to double death's door. The deck has your back. Trust it, and trust that no game is over until it's over.


Conclusion:


You have one job. Burn. Do not spend time entertaining or even considering your opponent's intentions, actions or feelings.


Just. Do. Damage.


Quickly and consistently lower their life total while leaving yourself some spells in hand as options for future plays.


If you want to play with feelings, play with water. If you want to play with finesse, play with air. If you want to play with muscle, play with earth. But if you want to leave your enemy in ashes, play with fire!


;0)


I hope that you enjoy playing this deck and your own variations. Please let me know how it goes for you when you try it? Looking forward to hearing from you and seeing you at an event sometime soon!



-UnderSietch

decks.primer:
Overview


The strategy is pretty straightforward: overwhelm your opponent in the early game with Earth's overstatted minions and then carry your advantage through the mid game with [[Avatar of Air]]'s mobility and Air's powerful magics.

Even without any Charge minions this deck hits hard and very fast, punishing any slow start or bricky hand from the opponent. Most of my games at the tournament were over before my opponent could manage to do anything meaningful.

Playing the deck requires good fundamentals of the game, especially site and minion placing, and being able to always plan a couple turns ahead with your avatar position.

The main way this deck loses is by being to greedy at the mulligan and bricking on threshold, so try to aim for a smooth hand that has a turn 2 and turn 3 play rather than hyperfocusing on getting a [[Pudge Butcher]] out on turn 3.



Tips and Tricks


Having a good grasp of some of the common play patterns of this deck can help better understand some of the building choices so I decided to include some tips on how to sequence and place your cards better.


-At the cost of sounding too obvious: ALWAYS place an Air site on turn 1, waste a Tower if you have to.

-One of the strongest plays of the deck is to play a double threshold site on turn 1, followed by an Earth site and a Tower to play a 4 drop on turn 3. This is obviously only possible if you open a double threshold site, so don't try to gamble for it.

-Try to to place your Air sites in a V shape, this way you have access to [[Avatar of Air]]'s ability in as many rows and columns as possible. This is especially important to be able to move again your [[Pudge Butcher]] if needed.

-In the early game it's usually best to cast your minions on top of you so you can fling them the following turn where they are most needed. Later in the game the choice isn't as obvious because you might need your minions in different positions to be able to block and you want to be able to fling [[Avatar of Air]] itself or to move it and fling something else if needed.

-After you have developed your sites you can start attacking with your avatar, especially if your opponent also has Air sites.

-If you're able to, try to space your non-Ordinary sites to make [[Atlantean Fate]] as bad as possible.



Card Choices


Artifacts

-[[Ring of Morrigan]]: this deck doesn't abuse it as much as others because you're casting only 1 spell each turn most of the time, however [[Avatar of Air]]'s mobility means you can always hit something meaningful with it and it's a great tool to deal the lethal blow.

-[[Grim Guisarme]]: playing a lot of high-statted minions means this card hits extra hard giving less time to the opponent and making healing often ineffective. You can also occasionaly combo it with [[Grapple Shot]] on the avatar for a surprise OTK.

-[[Rolling Boulder]]: I was originally playing 2 but after noticing that the deck can sometimes struggle against a wide board of small minions I decided to run the full set. It's fine to roll it once and just leave it there but I generally try to have it end up in a spot within reach so that my opponent has to play around it and most importantly can't steal it.


Minions

-[[Bosk Troll]]: the deck really wants to have a turn 2 play and this is the best option after [[Kettletop Leprechaun]].

-[[Kettletop Leprechaun]]: the best 2 drop available, being able to draw spell instead of site more often really helps offsetting the lack of draw power.

-[[Autumn Unicorn]]: an overstatted drop with no draw back is all the decks really wants, the double threshold can sometimes be tricky to handle but it's still worth playing it over the other options.

-[[Headless Haunt]]: same as [[Autumn Unicorn]] except having an Air threshold allows you to keep some hands where you cast it on turn 2 you otherwise would be forced to mulligan. During testing I was convinced the random teleport gave you a good result on average, but at the tournament I was particularly unlucky with the dice so I'm considering [[Belmotte Longbowmen]] as a replacement.

-[[Shield Maidens]]: I was initally not sold on playing an understatted minion in a deck that just wants to overwhelm the opponent with raw stats but after testing it became undeniable that this card gives excellent support against almost every matchup, even against decks that don't run [[Poison Nova]].

-[[Sir Bors the Younger]]: I already liked the card on its own but being able to move it around for free just makes it busted, having only 2 health is generally irrelevant.

-[[Dalcean Phalanx]]: once again an overstatted minion with an hardly relevant drawback.

-[[Pudge Butcher]]: the star of the deck, it's already strong outside of it but combining it with [[Avatar of Air]] makes it almost unstoppable and forces your opponent to keep feeding it minions to not get their avatar dragged.

-[[Sir Perceval]]: mostly a filler card since I wanted one more 4 drop, if you get it out very early you can force a situation where your opponent can't stop it from reaching its site but most of the time don't bother trying to get the draw.

-[[Daperyll Vampire]]: after the rules changes this card is just too good to not be played in every Air deck that reaches 5 mana.

-[[Sir Galahad]]: meant to be the 4th [[Daperyll Vampire]] but hasn't been amazing so far, could very well be replaced by a [[Hounds of Ondaros]].

-[[Riddle Sphinx]]: in my opinion one of the most underrated cards in the game right now. At worst it's a 4 power flyer that cycles itself, at best you have mulliganed at the bottom an impactful late game card like [[Earthquake]] or [[Whirling Blades]] and can trick your opponent into letting you draw it instead of a random card. It's been really helpful in squeezing out a little bit of extra gas in longer games.


Magics

-[[Browse]]: mostly a filler card but the threshold isn't very hard to get and it can help you find the right card to kill your opponent or deal with a tricky board. It can also set up the bottom for [[Riddle Sphinx]].

-[[Common Sense]]: while it's a tempo loss, being able to have extra copies of [[Dispel]], [[Bury]] and [[Grapple Shot]] in the deck without risking to brick on them is worth the 2 extra mana you have to spend. Getting a minion with it doesn't come up often.

-[[Dispel]]: it just feels necessary to run at least 1 to deal with [[Ring of Morrigan]], [[Jihad]], [[Atlantean Fate]] and other pesky cards.

-[[Bury]]: a spot removal that can double as artifact hate, it's true that there is a lot of Water going around recently but it hasn't been a problem yet.

-[[Grapple Shot]]: one of the best Air cards in the game, espacially in a deck full of high-statted minions like this. I realized at the time of writing this primer that I didn't draw a single copy during the tournament.

-[[Earthquake]]: as I said before for [[Rolling Boulder]] I wanted some ways to deal with wide boards, moving the sites around can also be very beneficial since the deck is very focused on positioning.

-[[Whirling Blades]]: it was initally at 2 copies because I feared bricking on it but I found it to be one of the best cards in the deck. It clears wide boards with no regards for Stealth, can increase your damage to end games faster and it's a great tool to deal the fatal blow.


Sites

You want to play as many Air sites as possible while keeping high enough chances to have 2 Earth sites by turn 4. I initially took the ratios from other topping [[Avatar of Air]] lists, then tweaked them a little because I found the deck can afford to run a low number of no-threshold sites and there are a couple I think are strong enough to justify the risk.


-[[Glastonbury Tor]], [[The Colour Out of Space]], [[Tintagel]], [[Valley of Delight]], [[Windmill]]: this deck simply can't work without running as many multi-element sites as possible, so to not lose to [[Atlantean Fate]] too hard you need to compensate by not playing many others non-Ordinary sites. Thankfully the deck doesn't really benefit from most of them anyway so it's not a big loss.

-[[Dark Tower]], [[Gothic Tower]], [[Lone Tower]]: they allow some of the strongest plays in your deck but can end up being wasted because of threshold so I don't play more copies, don't be greedy during the mulligan and get rid of them if you can't arrange a meaningful play without risking to brick on threshold.

-[[Hunter's Lodge]]: I don't think I've resolved its ability once during testing or at the tournament but the potential to counter [[Infiltrate]], [[Sir Agravaine]] and [[Morgana le Fay]] seems more valuable than a Foot Soldier.

-[[Lookout]]: I think the info on the opponent's hand is a little overrated but since I wanted an Air site to play on turn 1 if I don't get a multi-element one this is the only Ordinary option.

-[[Pebbled Paths]]: Charge is the strongest keyword in the game, so of course you wanna play the site that shuts it down.

-[[Pillar of Zeiros]]: it's often just an Earth site that does nothing but it's always good to have extra insurance against an aggro deck randomly opening nuts and running you down too fast.

-[[Wizard's Den]]: similar to [[Riddle Sphinx]] the extra card can be the difference between a won game and one that gets stolen right under your nose, being the aggressor in most matchups and emptying your hand generally quickly means you won't have to worry too much about having to discard a spell because of it.

-[[Sinkhole]]: the strongest site in the deck, why nobody else is playing it is beyond me. You can't be greedy with it in the mulligan but if you open an hand that allows you to use it on turn 2 or 3 while playing on curve you just automatically win. It can also help in the [[Archimago]] matchup by freeing the way from [[Gnome Hollows]] and [[Perilous Bridge]] or by messing with their threshold.



What's not here and why


-[[Onyx Core]]: while increasing your chances of reaching double Earth threshold is good and all, risking to draw a site when you need a spell in a deck that is already struggling with card draw isn't worth it.

-[[Torshammar Trinket]]: one of the most recent exclusions from the deck, the extra power was often not relevant enough and I was running too many cards that are dead if I don't already have a minion on the board.

-[[Blink]], [[Flanking Maneuver]] and other mobility cards: since this deck is heavily focused on tempo I don't want to use extra mana to do something my avatar does for free, with the exception of [[Headless Haunt]] I rarely find myself in spots where they would be useful.

-[[Crusade]]: the deck does run a lot of Earth minion but the extra power is often overkill and the minions in this deck don't really benefit from being summoned on your opponent's side of the board.

-[[Highland Falconer]], [[Palliburrie Bats]]: playing these or [[Bosk Troll]] is mostly a meta call, right now there are too many [[Vile Imp]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] around so I prefer having a single stronger minion. Deck space is also an issue.

-[[Highland Princess]]: an auto-inclusion if you're running [[Torshammar Trinket]] but not worth playing it with only 1 target in the deck.

-[[Hyter Sprites]]: could be another replacement for [[Bosk Troll]] to combo with [[Lookout]], I didn't have time to test it.

-[[Lightning Bolt]], [[Magic Missiles]]: the deck usually just runs over small creatures and doesn't need help in dealing the fatal blow.

-[[Belmotte Longbowmen]]: a possible replacement for [[Headless Haunt]], but has the big downside of being very reliant on [[Avatar of Air]] to be effective.

-[[Castle Haunt]]: might look fine on paper but not being able to move is a terrible drawback in practice.

-[[Feast for Crows]]: a strong effect but it's not worth the tempo loss and card disadvantage.

-[[Root Spider]]: the deck doesn't really need to worry about defending itself, playing them on the surface and then flinging them on an enemy an burrowing them can be a cool play tho.

-[[Chaos Twister]]: it should probably be in the deck over some combination of [[Earthquake]]/[[Rolling Boulder]]/[[Whirling Blades]], I just despise the mechanic and refuse to spend time to learn how to blow it consistently.

-[[Gigantism]]: it's a 3rd copy of [[Grim Guisarme]] that costs 1 mana more, didn't seem needed and increases the amount of cards that require a minion on the board to be relevant. (Please note that I'm biased by the fact that I kept drawing it when my opponent was already in DD during testing)

-[[Mask of Mayhem]]: not being able to control which minion attacks and when is too big of a drawback.

-[[Royal Bodyguard]]: the effect isn't needed often and I didn't need other 4 drops but it could replace [[Sir Perceval]].

-[[The Black Plague]]: ends up being just a clunky removal, the deck doesn't struggle against [[Root Spider]] enough to justify it.

-[[Hounds of Ondaros]]: I've seen a lot of people say this card is amazing but I have never tested it and I don't really see where the hype is, if you're not really sold on [[Riddle Sphinx]] (but you should be) this is the obvious replacement.

-[[Bower of Bliss]]: this is one of the other no-threshold sites I find powerful enought to play in your atlas, unfortunately that would mean giving up on [[Shield Maidens]] which is just too important.

-[[Cloud City]]: moving it around rarely accomplishes something so I'd rather play more ordinary sites.

-[[Common Village]], [[Humble Village]], [[Rustic Village]], [[Simple Village]]: they can be run over [[Hunter's Lodge]] but you can't play them on turn 1 and would rather use all your mana on the following turns.

-[[Kingdom of Agartha]]: turning off all your removals isn't worth it.

-[[Merlin's Tower]]: This deck only plays a couple of Magics and they're mostly situational so it's hard to arrange plays with it, better to just play more Ordinary sites instead.

-[[Mirror Realm]]: there aren't many strong sites to copy in the deck.

-[[Perilous Bridge]]: this site ends up being a problem for yourself more often than it is for your opponent, you generally would want to place it right in front of your avatar but that's where you usually need an Earth site.

-[[Rift Valley]]: the positional advantage isn't worth running a non-Ordinary site.



Tournament Report


Round 1 vs [[Deathspeaker]]: W

He tried his best to stall with [[Grain Sparrow]] and [[Bane Widow]] but ended up bricking on double [[Poison Nova]] against my [[Shield Maidens]].


Round 2 vs Earth Water Fire [[Sorcerer]]: W

It was an original build based around Mortals. A slow starting hand put him on the backfoot and then [[Whirling Blades]] killing [[Sir Agravaine]], [[Kingswood Poachers]] and [[Shield Maidens]] sealed the deal.


Round 3 vs Steam [[Druid]]: W

The game was single handedly won by turn 1 [[Ring of Morrigan]] completely shutting down Tawny. A well timed [[Sinkhole]] also helped in keeping him on the defensive.


Round 4 vs Fire Air [[Pathfinder]]: W

She hard bricked on threshold, I'm pretty sure the only spell she managed to cast for the entire game was a single [[Hamlet's Ablaze!]] right before losing.


Round 5 vs Mono FIre [[Druid]]: ID

We were both guaranteed in top so we decided to rest for a round and go get some coffee. I ended up being 1st in Swiss since both my round 3 and 4 opponent's made top cut.


Top 8 vs Air Earth [[Druid]]: W

I had a shaky start because I struggled to find a 2nd Earth site but my opponent bricked harder. He kept an heavy Air hand hoping to draw a 2nd Air site but didn't draw it until very late after I already hit the first one with [[Sinkhole]].


Top 4 vs [[Archimago]]: L

It's already a very hard matchup for the deck on average hands, but my opponent just made it impossible by opening [[Ring of Morrigan]], double [[Divine Healing]] and then drawing plenty of removal while I didn't see the cards I need most. Fortunately it was piloted by my best friend and testing partner @Solaris who ended up winning the whole thing so I didn't feel too bad about it.

decks.name: 1st Place Cornerstone Gothenburg - Waveshaper Control
decks.primer:
Waveshaper has been my go-to avatar since I started playing with the precons. The amount of control the tap ability provides and room for interesting plays with cards that synergies with the body of water makes every game feel fresh and unique.


Strategy

This is a control deck that aims to survive the first rounds with hindering sites ([[Perilous Bridge]], [[Tadpole Pool]], [[Troll Bridge]], [[Babbling Brook]]) and sticky minions. ([[Adept Illusionist]], [[Sir Tom Thumb]], [[Lugbog Cat]])


We accrue value with [[Highland Princess]], [[Grandmaster Wizard]] and [[Captain Baldassare]]. There are multiple ways to recast and regain these effects through [[Selfsame Simulacrum]], [[Fey Changeling]] and [[The Lady of the Lake]]. To make sure we are staying ahead in resources over our opponent we have [[Atlantean Fate]], [[The Great Drowning of Men]] and [[Wrath of the Sea]].


To get our opponent to death’s door we utilize evasive and hard to kill minions such as [[Gyre Hippogriffs]], [[Daperyll Vampire]], [[Hounds of Ondaros]], [[Questing Beast]], [[Mester Stoor Worm]], [[The Green Knight]] and [[Thundering Giant]].


Other Notable Cards

  • [[Plague of Frogs]] - Gum up the board (and potentially get a big life total swing together with [[Ruler of Thul]].
  • [[Pollimorph]] & [[Mesmerism]] - Remove/turn any pesky minions.
  • [[Stormy Seas]] - Submerge artifacts that give our opponent an edge or remove one or multiple minions.
  • [[Riptide]] - We can use it on our minions to protect them if we need to overextend, pull our enemies' minions or avatar to get to them or pull them aside to get an attack we otherwise couldn’t get through.
  • [[Watchtower]] & [[Hounds of Ondaros]] - Stealth is a very strong mechanic and we use these to being able to remove [[Infiltrate]] and letting us target [[Morgana le Fay]].


Highland Princess Jewel Box

The suite of artifacts are specifically chosen for the Highland Princess and the impact they can provide for the game. Depending when you play her and what other cards you have in hand/play, the decision can turn the game in your favor.  

  • [[Amethyst Core]] & [[Aquamarine Core]] - Stable choices to secure the threshold you need.
  • [[Mix Aer]] - Usually used to get a Grandmaster Wizard into play.
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]] & [[Torshammar Trinket]] - Great against aggressive decks when you need to make sure you can kill their minions without trading with your own.
  • [[Philosopher’s Stone]] - Great for the mid- and end-game when you would like to cast multiple spells.

decks.name: Dragonlord-Xeraphine Konrul (Cornerstone Oulu 2025, 2-2)
decks.primer:
The deck went 2-2 in Swiss in a 17-player Cornerstone event.


Game 1: Druid (fire/water). A quick 0-2 loss, not much I could achieve here.


Game 2: Druid (water/air). Lost game 1, but was able to squeeze a 2-1 victory with some good draws.


Game 3: Pathfinder (fire/air). Again, lost game 1, but won 2-1 in the end by getting to high mana and rotating strong uniques from the cemetery.


Game 4: Druid (water). Lost 0-2 in long, grindy matches. The opponent had lots of submerge effects, so I tried to dig for Icebergs, but failed. Maybe they could have turned one of the games. But there would have been no time for a game 3 so perhaps it was for the best.


Top 8: Druid (water/fire). Quickly lost 0-2. Pretty similar to the first match of the day. Steam Druid is just too fast and my deck had very limited ways to deal with a flipped Druid with Drums.


Conclusions:


Xeraphine takes a bit of time to get going, but if you are able to draw a strong unique (Morgana, Boudicca, etc) and play it over and over again, the deck can be very strong.


The key is to build the manabase up to 6-7 without delay. Then find a beefy unique. Play new minions instead of activating Xeraphine and only use left over mana for her ability. Remember that she also gives your Avatar flying which can be handy at times.


The three Drowns are a meta choice to submerge Drums from a flipped Druid, not meant for creature removal.


When sideboarding Autumn Rivers replace Icebergs if opponent doesn’t play water. The Drowns can be kept for creature removal or swapped for Shatter Strikes when not facing a Druid.


Warp Spasm is a pet card due to art. Another card would probably be better. The main deck Xeraphine Konryl should possibly also be a different card. And forgot to add 2x Ashkelon Phoenix to sidebord.


In casual play the deck is fun and does well againts most Avatars. In a tournament where 4/5 of my games were against Druids, the 2-2 finish was perhaps a bit overperforming.
